lesson_title: The Monthly Room Booking: How the Body Prepares for a Baby
hook_text: Your body books a room every single month for a guest who usually never shows up.
clip_script: Every month the uterus is a hotel room getting ready for a guest who may never arrive. Days 1 to 5: last month's unused carpet, the thick lining, is stripped out. That is the period. Days 6 to 13: oestrogen, the decorator, lays a fresh, thick, blood-rich carpet. Around day 14: an egg is released from the ovary and drifts down the oviduct. It lasts about a day. Days 15 to 28: progesterone, the manager, holds the booking. No guest? The manager goes home, the carpet comes down, day 1 again. But if a sperm meets that egg in the oviduct, 23 plus 23 chromosomes make one new cell. It doubles and doubles on its way down, and after about a week it moves in, burrowing into the carpet. Now it sends a message that keeps the manager at work, so there is no period. That message is what a pregnancy test detects. Nine months later, the guest checks out, head first.
visual_style: A cartoon hotel room inside a uterus outline; a calendar flips days 1 to 28 while a carpet is stripped, relaid and held; an egg drifts down a tube, meets a sperm and doubles into a ball that settles into the carpet.
pacing: Calendar-driven beats for each phase, a pause on the meeting, a quick doubling montage, a light final joke.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name the hormone for each phase of the cycle.
